title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Push-to-Talk Readback. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Push-to-Talk Readback
options.lineage: handheld aviation and field radios: PTT key, TX tally, channel LCD, the controller's readback
options.thesis: You key up, talk, release, and the words land. Refine is the readback: the same message, corrected, in place. Never 'say again'.
options.viewport: HUD is a slim graphite capsule under the menu bar: red TX tally + live level while keyed, amber 'decoding', green 'landed', then it shrinks to a 'Readback ⌥⌘R' pill in the corner. Main window: sidebar (Dictate, Files, Voice, Prompts, System), graphite shell, amber numerals for timers/model/latency only.
options.risk: Pushed too far it becomes a radio costume; held to palette, tally states, and amber numerals it stays a native Mac app.

raised.raise: One strict state vocabulary across HUD, menu bar and window: TX red, decoding amber, landed green, refining amber pulse, never reused for decoration.
The HUD shows exactly one thing at a time; each state fully replaces the last.
Numerals are tabular and measured: durations, latency, model size, nothing decorative.

options.label: Closed Captions
options.lineage: broadcast subtitles and CC line-21 captions
options.thesis: Your speech appears as a caption line, then gets set in place.
options.viewport: HUD is a caption bar at screen bottom; refine pill is a yellow caption chip.
options.risk: Familiar: most transcription UIs already lean on caption styling, and a bottom bar fights the Dock and the caret.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.case: Fuses poorly: dictation has no routes or network to map.
options.kept: A disciplined state vocabulary used identically everywhere.

options.label: Emigre Bitmap Specimen
options.case: Fuses poorly: a poster face fights a HUD that must stay small and calm.
options.kept: Nothing transferable to a working tool.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: Fuses poorly: full-viewport ownership is exactly what a non-obstructive HUD refuses.
options.kept: One state owns the HUD at a time.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.case: Fuses poorly: no audience link to dictation.
options.kept: Fixed scale across stages: the HUD keeps one height through every state.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.case: Holds audience identification (recording, sides, running time) but handwriting hurts clarity in a utility HUD.
options.risk: Reads as nostalgia, not a tool.

options.label: Datamatics
options.case: Fuses poorly: strobing black-white fields are hostile in a HUD over your work.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A native macOS utility: system materials, accent blue, SF Symbols, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar settings window and a translucent HUD like the system dictation bubble.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other Mac dictation app by design.
